cases.excerpt: Prostate cancer cases diagnosed between 2003 and 2008 which met with the inclusion criteria were included in the study. One hundred and twelfth (112) pairs of cases and controls matched by age and ethnicity were analysed.

effect_size.excerpt: Significantly reduced risks of prostate cancer were noted among those consuming more vegetables (OR= 0.12, 95% CI= 0.02-0.84), more tomatoes (OR= 0.35, 95% CI= 0.13-0.93) and those who had frequent sexual intercourse (OR= 0.44, 95% CI= 0.19-0.96).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Significantly reduced risks of prostate cancer were noted among those consuming more vegetables (OR= 0.12, 95% CI= 0.02-0.84), more tomatoes (OR= 0.35, 95% CI= 0.13-0.93) and those who had frequent sexual intercourse (OR= 0.44, 95% CI= 0.19-0.96).

validated_results.title: Dietary patterns and risk of advanced prostate cancer: a principal component analysis in Uruguay.
validated_results.reason: Original case-control principal component analysis reporting a Western dietary pattern odds ratio for newly diagnosed advanced prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: high quartile versus low quartile of the Western diet
extraction.population: Uruguayan men newly diagnosed with advanced prostate cancer and hospitalized controls

sample_size.excerpt: In order to explore the role of broader eating patterns in the etiology of prostate cancer, we conducted a principal components analysis among Uruguayan men. The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 345 + 690 = 1035

cases.excerpt: The study included 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Whereas the traditional and Western patterns were directly associated with risk of prostate cancer (OR for high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet was 2.35, 95% CI 1.44-3.85, p-value for trend < 0.0001), the prudent, drinker, and substituter patterns were not associated with risk of the disease.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Whereas the traditional and Western patterns were directly associated with risk of prostate cancer (OR for high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet was 2.35, 95% CI 1.44-3.85, p-value for trend < 0.0001), the prudent, drinker, and substituter patterns were not associated with risk of the disease.

comparison.excerpt: high quartile versus the low quartile of the Western diet

timing.excerpt: 345 newly diagnosed cases of advanced prostate cancer and 690 hospitalized controls

continent.excerpt: the high incidence of advanced prostate cancer in Uruguay

location.excerpt: a principal component analysis in Uruguay

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The factor analysis was performed using the control population. Factor analysis allowed the extraction of five patterns, labeled as prudent, traditional, substituter, drinker, and Western.
